title: PHI Passive House Classic
markLabel: Certified Passive House, Passive House Institute

rows.label: Cooling + Dehumidification Demand
rows.fallback: Set per project in PHPP

note: The original PHI standard, with very low heating and cooling demand limits. In some climates these limits are impractical to reach.

title: PHI Low Energy Building

rows.label: Cooling + Dehumidification Demand
rows.fallback: Set per project in PHPP

note: Close to the Classic standard, with a higher heating demand limit and a higher airtightness limit. It suits smaller buildings and often lets the design team avoid high solar-gain glazing, which helps comfort and summer performance.

rows.label: Renewable Primary Energy (PER) Demand
rows.fallback: Set per project in PHPP

note: PHI's standard for existing buildings where the new-construction limits are not practical. Under the component method, each assembly, the windows, and the ventilation system meet limits set by the climate zone. A retrofit done in stages can be pre-certified with an EnerPHit Retrofit Plan.

note: The same retrofit standard, met through a whole-building heating demand limit set by the climate zone instead of limits on each component. A retrofit done in stages can be pre-certified with an EnerPHit Retrofit Plan.

title: Phius CORE Prescriptive 2024

rows.label: Envelope and Equipment
rows.value: Per the Phius prescriptive checklist for the climate zone

note: A Phius CORE path that replaces the energy model with a checklist of envelope and equipment requirements. It carries a tighter airtightness limit and gives no credit for renewable energy.
